content_preview.title: mise v2026.10.19 Narrows Project Trust, Enforces Checksum and SLSA Verification and Makes lockfile_mode generate the Default
content_preview.summary: mise release v2026.10.19, published October 24, narrows what counts as project trust, enforces pinned checksums and SLSA provenance, and makes lockfile_mode generate the default, with a list of breaking changes.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The mise project published release v2026.10.19 on October 24, 2026. According to the [release notes](https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/tag/v2026.10.19), "Most of this release closes ways an untrusted repository, download host or mirror could run code, leak credentials or get around verification." The notes add that "Some of these fixes make mise stricter, so check **Breaking Changes** before you upgrade." Also in the release, per the [same notes](https://github.com/jdx/mise/relea...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, Trust, Install verification, Resource limits and credentials, Lockfile default, Breaking Changes Listed, Related Earlier Release, What We Don't Know). 871 words, within the News range of 400-1200. Appropriate technical depth for a developer-tools audience; the breaking-changes list is explicitly labelled a selection.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources are first-party GitHub release pages of jdx/mise (github.com is on config/source_allowlist.txt, line 1131); no independent coverage exists and the article says so. Snapshots read: source-0.html.gz (v2026.10.19, HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns) and source-1.html.gz (v2026.10.15, HTTP 200, no suspicious_patterns). Snapshot sanity check passed (each ~235 KB, contains the release body text; datetime 2026-10-24T20:02:03Z and 2026-10-19T10:19:30Z). Live re-fetch via GitHub API (repos/jdx/mise/releases/tags/<tag>) returned bodies matching the snapshots. Release date: v2026.10.19 tag/commit created 2026-10-24T16:18:02Z, published_at 2026-10-24T20:02:03Z; the article states October 24, 2026 as the publish date, correct under either reading (same calendar day UTC). v2026.10.19 verified: intro quotes 'Most of this release closes ways an untrusted repository, download host or mirror could run code, leak credentials or get around verification.' and 'Some of these fixes make mise stricter, so check Breaking Changes before you upgrade.' are verbatim; lockfile_mode = generate default, mise lsp semantic highlighting and {{ mise_config_dir }} all in the intro/Added. Trust section (help output, shim, hook, MCP, set/unset/tasks add; sibling config prompt; MCP refusals; forged worktree/symlink/.mise clone/.miserc.toml; TAB completers) matches Security > Trust and safe mode (#14903, #14902, #14898). Hook quote 'a directory name containing {{ exec(...) }} could run code from a cd hook.' verbatim (#14897). Install verification quote 'Pinned checksums, Node signatures, SLSA provenance (including the tag it was built from) and GitHub attestations are now enforced. Before, a 404 or a missing file could make mise skip them.' verbatim from Highlights; checksum enforcement for erlang, npm, spm and http, missing SHASUMS256.txt.sig failing the install (#14899), different-tag SLSA rejection with verbatim quote 'a mirror can't serve an older release's genuine artifact and provenance as a newer version.' (#14924), backdated GitLab released_at and no-transparency-log bundles vs minimum_release_age (#14912) all confirmed. Limits: 128 MiB HTTP cap, extraction stops past 256 MiB AND 100x download size, extract_max_ratio global-only (Added), symlink restriction for github/http/aqua/cargo-binstall/packslip/vfox (#14895, #14915) confirmed. Credentials: GitHub token only to GitHub API hosts or api_url; credentials kept out of install dir names, manifests, mise.lock, Referer headers, logs, error messages (#14913, #14917) confirmed. Lockfile paragraph matches the Changed entry (#14893) including merge opt-out and MISE_LOCKFILE_MODE=merge. Breaking Changes: 'Most setups need no changes' verbatim; Node (.sig mirrors, 4.0.0 and 5.12.0, node.gpg_verify = false), GitHub Enterprise, Archives (brew casks and aqua dmg/pkg exempt, extract_max_ratio or 0), Worktrees, Task sandbox (Linux before 6.2, io_uring under --deny-net), Hooks (project root) all verbatim in substance. Attribution: every item is in the v2026.10.19 body it is attributed to. v2026.10.15 (published 2026-10-19, 'a few days earlier' = 5 days, fine): 24-hour minimum_release_age 'used to cover only backends that reported release dates', now every backend, 'no versions found' (verbatim, in quote marks in source), minimum_release_age_excludes opt-out and '0s' to disable all confirmed. Title claims: 'Narrows Project Trust' (Highlight: 'Trust is narrower'), 'Enforces Checksum and SLSA Verification' (Highlight: 'Verification fails closed'; enforcement is default behaviour, with listed escape hatches such as node.gpg_verify = false), 'lockfile_mode generate the Default' (Changed) are each supported. Not stated by the article: contributor credits and the first-time contributors; no issue. The article does not claim mise is first to adopt cooldowns, so no inconsistency with the Herald's dependency-cooldowns Analysis (2026-10/24). Prompt-injection scan: suspicious_patterns null for both sources; nothing found. Independent-source count not applicable (News).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number (128 MiB, 256 MiB, 100x, 24 hours, Linux 6.2, versions 4.0.0 and 5.12.0), date, setting name and quote traces to the cited release body. No misattribution between v2026.10.19 and v2026.10.15. Minor: the article says the notes list 'further specifics' under a quote that actually comes from the Highlights; immaterial. The claim that the Herald found no independent reporting is a statement about the Herald's own search and was not independently checked; it is plausible and appropriately hedged.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, attributes every claim to the release notes; includes an explicit What We Don't Know section noting no evidence of exploitation and that the Herald did not test the release.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald article covers mise. Related context: the Herald's dependency-cooldowns Analysis (2026-10/24) and GitHub Dependabot cooldown article (2026-07/20) cover the cooldown topic generally, but mise is not covered there; not duplicative.
recommendations: Single-vendor sourcing is inherent to a release-notes story; a later follow-up could add independent security commentary if any appears.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed first-party release coverage with all quotes verbatim, correct release dating and correct release-by-release attribution. Approved without corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate security-hardening release coverage for a defined developer-tools audience, single first-party source
